intentAndPurpose.intent: Display a user or entity representation as image, icon, or text initials.

props.name: alt
props.description: Alt text / name used for accessibility and initials extraction

props.name: attention
props.description: Attention level — High (filled), Medium (tinted), Low (transparent). Default: 'high'

props.name: content
props.description: Display content: image, icon, or text (initials). Aligns with Figma property `content`.

props.name: customSize
props.description: Custom diameter in pixels when `size='custom'`. Defaults to 60 to match the Figma custom specimen (node 31:134).

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test automation id — forwarded to the root element.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Custom fallback content when image fails or for icon/text content

props.name: onPress
props.description: Click handler — when set, the avatar renders as an interactive Base UI button.

props.name: src
props.description: Image source URL (when content is image)

codeSnippets.title: Basic Usage
codeSnippets.code:
import { Avatar } from '@oneui/ui';

<Avatar src="/photo.jpg" alt="Jane Doe" />

interactionBehavior.summary: Avatar is presentational by default — a non-focusable `<span role="img">` with no hover, press, or focus paint. Passing `onPress` or `onClick` is what flips it: the root becomes a Base UI `<button>`, `cursor: pointer` appears, and keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo. There is still no hover or pressed fill, and no tap-scale, so the only visual acknowledgement of a click is that native button activation (plus the halo if you tabbed there).
focus: Only the interactive variant (`onPress` / `onClick` set) is focusable — it is a real `<button>`. The default `<span>` is not in the tab order.

Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring (spread is `--Stroke-XL` + `--Focus-Outline-Width`), so it stays legible inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
`:focus` alone clears the native outline — the visible indicator is `:focus-visible` only, so a mouse click does not paint a ring.
keyboard: The interactive variant is a native `<button type="button">`, so `Enter` and `Space` both activate it with no custom key handling.
`handleActivate` no-ops when `disabled`, and the native `disabled` attribute is set, so the click / key handlers never fire.
A presentational Avatar (no `onPress` / `onClick`) cannot be focused or activated from the keyboard.
disabled: Dims to `--Avatar-disabledOpacity` (falls back to `--Disabled-Opacity`) on both the presentational and interactive roots.
The CSS sets `cursor: not-allowed` but does **not** set `pointer-events: none` — the interactive variant is a native `<button disabled>`, which already blocks activation on its own.

On that native disabled button, browsers ignore `cursor`, so `not-allowed` is not actually observable; the pointer shows the parent's cursor. This is the known system-wide gap (see docs/design/disabled-states.md). The presentational `<span>` has no `pointer-events: none`, so `not-allowed` can show there.
There is no loading state, and `disabled` does not imply one.
touch: There is no hover fill and no press fill or tap-scale, so a finger tap on an interactive Avatar has no painted acknowledgement — only the native button click.
The whole circular root is the hit target; there is no inner control to miss.
